**Module 3 objectives**

This module introduces widely used techniques for analysing multivariate biological data. By the end of this module, you will be able to:

- Understand the principles underlying **Principal Components Analysis (PCA)** and **Non-metric Multidimensional Scaling (nMDS)**
- Be familiar with the concepts behind **multivariate hypothesis testing** using **permutational techniques** such as **ANOSIM** and **PERMANOVA**
- Be able to **plan and conduct experiments** that test multivariate hypotheses
- Know how to **carry out these analyses using relevant statistical software**
- Be able to **interpret, present, and report** your findings clearly and effectively

:::

## Introduction

For these practicals you will continue working on your own group data, with demonstrators on hand to help:

- **Week 12:** Carry out additional analyses, summarise your findings, and review guidance on describing multivariate methods and results in your report.
- **Week 13:** Work with demonstrators on Report 2 analyses and reporting, or use the practical for exam revision. This is a scheduled practical and attendance will be recorded.

## Week 12: Additional analyses and reporting

Use the [Report 2 required analysis checklist](../assessments/assessment-report-2.qmd#required-analysis-checklist) to identify any outstanding analyses and outputs. Demonstrators will help you analyse and interpret your data, including ANOVAs of habitat PC scores and regressions relating those scores to selected species measures, and discuss how to describe your methods and results.

## Week 13: Report support and exam revision

**Week 13 is a scheduled practical. Attend your allocated class and record your attendance as usual. The usual practical attendance requirement applies.**

You can work with demonstrators to finalise your Report 2 analyses and reporting, or ask questions and revise for the exam with your tutors and peers. If you have finished your report, use the practical for exam revision.

## Before submitting Report 2

Check the [required analyses and outputs](../assessments/assessment-report-2.qmd#required-analysis-checklist) and [marking scheme](../assessments/assessment-report-2.qmd#marking-scheme) on the [Report 2 instructions page](../assessments/assessment-report-2.qmd), which contains the full report, presentation and submission requirements.

Your report should explain how the analyses address your hypotheses, rather than simply reproduce software output. Use these practicals to resolve outstanding analyses and questions about reporting.
